The `value` attribute is the default (form reset restores it); the property is the current value. In slotted-input mode it reads and writes the author's input.
Upstream onChange runs on every edit, which is the native `input` event; the native `change` fires once when the edit is committed (blur or Enter). Neither fires on property writes.
`(value, event) => void | Promise<void>` after each user edit; busy (:state(busy), aria-busy, spinner) while a returned promise is pending.

keyboard.action: Clears, fires tct-clear (cancelable), input and change, and restores focus to the input synchronously.

form.notes: Form-associated (ElementInternals): submits `name=value`, resets to the `value` attribute, restores on navigation, joins <fieldset disabled>, works with form= and label for. Validation shows after a commit, a blur after an edit or a submit attempt, never on form.checkValidity(). Slotted-input mode submits the author's own <input> exactly once and adds no entry of its own.

differences.text: Uncontrolled by default: `value` is a property with the `value` attribute as its default, and the native `input`/`change` events report edits, instead of a controlled value plus onChange. Set the property to control it.

Slotted-input mode (`<input slot="input">`) lets password managers, autofill and browser form restoration see a native field; label, description and status are light-DOM satellites wired with ids. The input owns name, value, type, required, disabled and autocomplete there.
`minlength`, `maxlength` and `pattern` are additions (native constraints that take part in validity). `type` also accepts search, tel and url.

Invalidity shows only after user interaction, on one clock: `:state(user-invalid)` and `aria-invalid` flip together, the browser's message becomes the status (frozen while typing, announced once), and a failed submit focuses the field.
The tooltip status variant is a focusable button with a name ("Error details", "Warning details"...) rather than a hover-only icon.

Outlined field from the Tecton input tokens (border, hover, focus ring in hot pink through the shared focus-ring module, 4px element radius); the label does not change colour on focus and status messages are ink without a wash (tecton-astryx components.ts, textfield.md).
The `input-group` label context (a label shown once for a group of fields) needs an element from WP-7 and is not wired: inside a group the field only drops its own box chrome (`data-in-group`).
Tier 2 (no element reflection): a host `aria-describedby` is not merged into a shadow input's description; label, description and status are still exposed by text fallback.

provisional: Adornment sizes, and the status tooltip variant's glyph position, follow the Tecton field tokens but were not compared with a Tecton design frame (textfield.md gives no adornment spec).

requests.reason: The CEM target check should accept global attributes as targets (`autofocus` for hasAutoFocus); the CEM does not list them for the element.

formData()/entries()/values() read `new FormData(form)` after the submit; a tct-button submitter is a temporary native button, so its entry is not in it. The contract tests capture `new FormData(form, event.submitter)` inside the submit event. Consider a harness helper (`submissions()`).

core.text-input.notes: Guides: [mwg:form-associated-custom-elements] ElementInternals value, validity, reset and restore; [mwg:validate-input-after-interaction] user-invalid timing; [mwg:required-field-feedback] indicators are text; [mwg:accessible-error-announcement] the status is announced once; [mwg:ime-safe-enter-submit] Enter is ignored while composing; [mwg:custom-button-actions] the clear button restores focus.
